meta.title: AlarmTalk · The one alarm that changes your morning
meta.description: Forget the beeping. Wake up to the real voice of someone you love — at the exact time, every time.

hero.badge: A voice alarm app, made in Korea

hero.waitlistHint: Before launch — join the beta waitlist

items.title: Native alarm
items.body: Not a push notification. Rings on time even with the screen locked or in airplane mode.

items.title: AI-generated voice
items.body: A real recording from a real person. Not the polished perfection of synthetic voice — the living tone that wakes you.

items.title: kinds of voices
items.body: Voices you record yourself, voices shared from someone, and translated phrases for language practice.

voice.description: Adding a hundred more bell sounds still gives you the same noise. The moment a real human voice wakes you up, everything changes.
voice.bullet1: Record a line for the day — workout, exam, or trip
voice.bullet2: Schedule a different voice for each context
voice.bullet3: Voices you record once get reused across alarms

shared.description: Use a share code to collect voices from family, partner, or friends. A week of greetings, each in a slightly different tone, stack up in your library.
shared.bullet1: Share voices with family or partner via invite code
shared.bullet2: Received voices live safely in your own library

language.description: Set today's memorized sentence as tomorrow's alarm. Five seconds groggily heard each day adds up to 35 minutes of practice a week.
language.bullet1: Set foreign-language phrases in a native voice
language.bullet2: Perfect for the month before a trip
language.bullet3: Swap in new sentences as you progress

scenarios.headline: Some people use it like this.
scenarios.description: AlarmTalk redesigns the first second of every morning, not just the alarm sound.

items.title: Apart on weekends
items.body: Recorded after work: “Good night. See you tomorrow morning.” Plays every day at 7:30 sharp.

items.title: A note to your future self
items.body: “The you in three months is grateful for the you who got up today.” Recorded yesterday, played this morning.

items.title: A grandmother waking her granddaughter
items.body: She sends a fresh recording every week. Greetings stack up, each in a slightly different tone.

items.title: Listening practice before a trip
items.body: Today's sentence becomes tomorrow's alarm. Five seconds a day adds up to 35 minutes a week.

items.q: Is it a push notification or a real alarm?
items.a: A real native alarm. Even with the screen locked or in airplane mode, it rings exactly on time. No reliance on server pushes.
Recordings stay tied to your account until you delete them. Voices you share live only in the recipient's library.
Core alarm and voice features will be free. Some things — extra cloud storage, translation, premium voices — will be in a paid tier.
Android native first. iOS follows once we've validated AlarmKit separately.

items.q: How is it different from other alarm apps?
items.a: Other apps add more sounds. AlarmTalk redefines an alarm as a person's voice. Who's speaking is the feature.
